report_name: Akamai Report: AI Scams Surge, Phishing Lifespan Shrinks

threat_actors.name: AI-driven Scam Operators
threat_actors.description: A class of threat actors who leverage AI and Phishing-as-a-Service (PhaaS) platforms to conduct online scams and phishing campaigns at high speed and scale, as described in Akamai's 'AI-Driven Digital Deception' report.
threat_actors.goals: To conduct online scams, including fake retail sites and fraudulent job postings, and credential theft through phishing.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Used as the core technique for online scams and credential theft, with its implementation now being highly automated and scaled using AI and Phishing-as-a-Service (PhaaS) platforms.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: The use of links to malicious sites is a central component of the phishing and online scams discussed in the report.

attack_patterns.name: Acquire Infrastructure: Domains
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors use automated toolkits for the rapid, bulk registration of domains as a key enabler of the accelerated phishing attack lifecycle.

attack_patterns.name: Fast Flux DNS
attack_patterns.description: Attackers use 'fast-flux' techniques to quickly rotate their infrastructure, helping them evade blocklists and security vendor detection.

tools.name: Phishing-as-a-Service (PhaaS)
tools.description: Automated platforms that handle the entire phishing lifecycle, from creating lures and websites to harvesting credentials. These services lower the barrier to entry for cybercrime and enable attacks at unprecedented scale and speed.

tools.name: Artificial Intelligence
tools.description: Leveraged by threat actors to generate more convincing and personalized phishing emails, social media posts, and website content, making them harder for users to detect.

identities.name: High-technology companies
identities.description: The most impersonated sector (41.6%) in AI-driven scams and phishing campaigns, with their brands used to lend credibility to scams.

identities.name: Financial services companies
identities.description: A heavily targeted sector (18.9%) for impersonation in AI-driven scams and phishing.

identities.name: Commerce companies
identities.description: A targeted sector (8.4%) for impersonation in AI-driven scams and phishing.

infrastructure.name: Automated Phishing Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Rapidly deployed and rotated infrastructure, including phishing sites and backend systems, managed by PhaaS toolkits to evade detection. The average lifespan of this infrastructure is noted as 22 days.

indicators.name: URL with Long Randomized String
indicators.pattern:
title: URL with Long Randomized String
id: 7c5b9d1e-f8a2-4b3c-9d1e-8a7b6c5d4e3f
status: experimental
description: Detects URLs containing long, potentially randomized strings in the path, which can be indicative of automated phishing or scam toolkits.
references:
  - https://www.ir.akamai.com/news-releases/news-release-details/akamai-report-ai-driven-digital-deception-escalating-enterprise
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-30
tags:
  - attack.t1566.002
level: medium
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate web applications that use long unique identifiers or session tokens in URL paths.
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri|re: '/[a-zA-Z0-9\-_=]{30,}'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects URLs containing long, potentially randomized strings in the path, a pattern associated with automated phishing toolkits as mentioned in the 'Cyber Observables' section of the report.
